applies_to: Private renting in England (rules differ in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland)
disclaimer: General guidance, not legal advice. Rules change, so follow the GOV.UK links. For help with a problem, contact Shelter or Citizens Advice.

questions.question: Is everyone living in the flat a full-time student?
questions.help: Full-time usually means a course of at least 1 year and at least 21 hours of study a week.

questions.question: Are energy bills (gas and electricity) included in your rent?
Will you watch live TV on any channel, or use BBC iPlayer?
questions.help: Netflix, YouTube and other on-demand streaming don't count.

questions.question: Are you in the UK on a visa (for example a Student visa)?

items.title: Check your deposit is protected
items.why: Your landlord must put your deposit in a government-approved scheme within 30 days, and give you the scheme details within 30 days. Protected deposits are much easier to get back.
steps: Ask your landlord or agent which scheme they used, or wait for the scheme details (they must arrive within 30 days).
Check it yourself with the scheme: Deposit Protection Service, MyDeposits or Tenancy Deposit Scheme.
Keep your move-in report from this app with your deposit paperwork. It's your evidence of the flat's condition.

links.label: GOV.UK – Information landlords must give you
GOV.UK – If your landlord doesn't protect your deposit

items.title: Get your safety documents and written terms
items.why: Your landlord must give you a copy of the gas safety record before you move in, and you have the right to see the Energy Performance Certificate (EPC). For tenancies starting on or after 1 May 2026, the landlord must give you the key terms in writing.
steps: Ask for the gas safety record (if the flat has gas).
Ask to see the EPC.
Check there is a working smoke alarm on each floor.
Keep your written tenancy terms somewhere safe.

items.title: Know your new renting rights (from May 2026)
items.why: Since 1 May 2026, new private tenancies in England roll on with no fixed end date, and some landlord practices are banned.
steps: After signing, your landlord can ask for at most 1 month's rent in advance.
You can end the tenancy by giving 2 months' notice in writing.
Rent can go up at most once a year, not in the first 12 months, with at least 2 months' notice.

links.label: GOV.UK – Renters' Rights Act overview for tenants

items.title: Prove your right to rent
items.why: Landlords in England must check that every adult tenant has the right to rent. If you have an eVisa, you prove it with a share code. Halls of residence are exempt.
steps: Get a right to rent share code from your UKVI account.
Send the share code and your date of birth to your landlord or agent.

links.label: GOV.UK – Prove your right to rent

items.title: Claim your council tax student exemption
items.when: As soon as you get a council tax bill
items.why: If everyone in the household is a full-time student, you don't have to pay council tax, but you usually have to tell the council.
steps: Ask your university for a council tax exemption certificate (proof you're a full-time student).
Find your local council with your postcode and apply for the exemption.

links.label: GOV.UK – Apply for a council tax discount

items.title: Set up council tax
items.why: Not everyone in your household is a full-time student, so a council tax bill will be issued. You may still get a discount.
steps: Find your local council with your postcode and tell them you've moved in.
Check which discounts you can claim (students in the household may still reduce the bill).

links.label: GOV.UK – Apply for a council tax discount

items.title: Set up gas and electricity
items.why: You pay from the day you move in, so start with an accurate meter reading and don't pay for the last tenant's energy.
steps: Take a dated photo of each meter reading on move-in day.
Find your gas supplier with your postcode on Find My Supplier.
For electricity, find your network operator first, then search their site for your supplier.
Contact the supplier, tell them you've moved in, and give them your readings.

links.label: Energy Networks Association – find your network operator (electricity)
Citizens Advice – find your energy supplier

items.title: Buy a TV licence
items.when: Before you watch live TV or BBC iPlayer
items.why: You need a TV licence (£180 a year) to watch or record live TV on any channel or service, or to use BBC iPlayer. In shared houses, check whether each room needs its own.
steps: Buy it online from TV Licensing (linked from GOV.UK).

items.title: Register with a GP (doctor)
items.when: In your first few weeks, before you get ill
items.why: Registering is free. You don't need proof of address, ID or immigration status.
steps: Search for GP surgeries near your new address on the NHS website.
Register online (about 15 minutes) or ask the surgery for a form.

links.label: NHS – How to register with a GP surgery

items.title: Register to vote (if you're eligible)
items.why: British, Irish and qualifying Commonwealth citizens can register in England, plus some EU citizens. Check the eligibility rules on GOV.UK.
steps: Check if you're eligible, then register online with your new address.
